fact: TechReviewAfrica reports PAPSS is now available to customers of I&M Bank Kenya, who can send money across participating African markets in Kenyan shillings through branches.
Kenya is on PAPSS: the central bank joined in September 2023, KCB went live in March 2025 and Pesalink plugged into PAPSS in February 2026, per tech-ish.
Through the Pesalink link to PAPSS, mobile money wallets in Kenya became a valid destination for inbound African payments, and Pesalink is piloted for termination of PAPSS transactions, per tech-ish.
TechCabal says Pesalink, Kenya's instant payments network, is linking local banks and mobile money providers to PAPSS.
Zepz says its core Sendwave remittance services in Kenya operate as normal, and Wise says customers abroad can send money to Kenyan shilling accounts and wallets such as M-PESA.

Connecting Africa reports Safaricom extended M-Pesa Global to Ethiopia in October 2024, so M-Pesa wallets in Kenya and Ethiopia can make cross-border transfers, and M-Pesa customers can send and receive in over 190 countries.

In a speech published 13 March 2026, the National Bank of Rwanda says the Central Bank of Kenya and National Bank of Rwanda signed an MoU on a licence passporting framework letting payment service providers licensed at home operate in the other state, on a Letter of No Objection from the sending authority.
